report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a lexical/content bias difference (B minus A) rather than something like syntax or temperature — Model B is shifted toward professional/academic and culinary/restaurant vocabulary early in the sequence.

Why I believe this
- Layer/position norm pattern: the difference is concentrated in late layers (layers ~10–25) and especially at early token positions (pos1–pos4). That pattern is typical of a change that affects final output preferences (logit-level choices) rather than low-level encoding.
- Logit-lens tokens: the top candidate tokens the difference vectors point toward are repeatedly in a small set of domains:
  - Academic/professional: "dissertation", "professional", "Professional", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "Hon", "honors", "Engineering", "technical", "preventive", "molecular", "professionalism"
  - Culinary / restaurants: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Cooking", "cooking", "baking", "Chef", "Kitchen", "Cook", "baker", "kitchen", "baked"
  - Some commercial/affluent/occupation tokens: "billionaire", "macroeconomic", "metropolitan", "multinational", "polyurethane", "petrochemical"
- Consistency: many cells across many late layers point to the same clusters of tokens (dissertation/restaurant/professional/cooking), indicating a repeated, coherent shift rather than noise.

What I do not claim
- I cannot precisely name the training objective that produced the change (e.g., whether B was fine-tuned on restaurant/career content or had different data balance). The evidence supports a change in token-preference toward those semantic domains but does not uniquely identify how that change was induced.
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here, so I cannot show concrete changed continuations; the logit-lens + norm pattern is the basis for this interpretation.

Short summary: Model B (relative to A) moves late-layer early-position residual activations toward vocabulary associated with professional/academic and culinary/restaurant topics, implying B will more often continue with words about "dissertation/professional/restaurant/cooking" in relevant contexts.
